packageRules.description: Every update (major, minor, patch, pins, overrides, CI runtimes) lands in one PR so the whole dependency set moves together and is validated against every workspace at once.
typescript stays on the 6.x compiler API (typescript-eslint, nest build, Next and api-extractor cannot load 7); the 7.x compiler arrives through the @typescript/native alias.

The docs job stays on its runner and Node: the diagram check compares against SVGs rendered by that image's Graphviz, and Mintlify refuses Node 25 and later. The sdk row's Node 22 is the SDK's engines.node floor on purpose, so it moves with engines.node, not with Node releases.

typescript-minimum is the oldest TypeScript the SDK's published declarations are checked against (packages/sdk/scripts/pack-check.ts, README Requirements). It is a measured floor, not a version to keep current: it moves only when pack:check fails against it and the README, docs and MINIMUM_TYPESCRIPT move with it.

Automerge disabled everywhere - this project closes accounts irreversibly, and CONTRIBUTING.md already asks for closer review on anything security-sensitive. A dependency bump is reviewed like any other change, never merged unattended.
Security fixes bypass the weekly schedule and PR concurrency limit - waiting until Monday for a vulnerable dependency defeats the point of scanning for one.
